pageInfo.subtitle: Develop flawless synchronization, pick-slanting mechanics, inside/outside string transitions, and effortless high-speed articulation.
pageInfo.heroDescription: Alternate picking is the absolute bedrock of guitar virtuosity. From Paul Gilbert and John Petrucci to Al Di Meola and Steve Morse, the ability to strike strings with strict, alternating downstrokes and upstrokes provides crystalline clarity, rhythmic authority, and unlimited speed. In this masterclass, you will demystify pick-slanting physics, eliminate string-hopping tension, master inside versus outside picking traps, and build bulletproof two-hand synchronization across the entire fretboard.

items.text: Wrist Deviation Over Forearm Rotation: Power your picking motion primarily from the wrist joint (side-to-side deviation) rather than rigid, fatiguing elbow hammering.
Pick Slanting & Escape Angles: Tilting the pick slightly upward (USX) or downward (DSX) allows the pick to escape the string plane cleanly without getting trapped.
Minimal Pick Depth: Expose only 1–2 mm of the pick tip; digging too deeply into the strings creates massive mechanical drag and destroys stroke recovery.
Edge Picking Angle: Angling the pick blade 15–20 degrees against the string slices cleanly through the metal with zero scraping resistance and a thick, punchy tone.
Dynamic Grip Pressure: Hold the pick firmly enough that it does not rotate, but keep your thumb, wrist, and forearm muscles loose and relaxed to avoid tendon strain.
The Two-Hand Synchrony Principle: The pick stroke and the fret-hand finger strike must collide at the exact microsecond; any timing gap produces muted or ghost notes.
Inside vs. Outside Picking: Outside picking (downstroke on lower string, upstroke on higher string) feels radically different from inside picking; practice both equally.
3NPS Reversing Cycle: 3-note-per-string scales force pick direction to flip on every string crossing; internalizing this alternating stroke flip is crucial for fast scale runs.
Micro-Burst Speed Training: Practice rapid 4-note or 6-note bursts at high tempo followed by a sustained resting note to train fast-twitch muscle fibers without tension fatigue.
Metronome Subdivisions: Practice strictly across 16th-note, sextuplet, and 32nd-note subdivisions, ensuring each downbeat locks squarely into the metronome click.

exercises.title: The Single-String Synchronization Engine (Frets 5-8)
exercises.description: Before adding complex string crossings, calibrate your two-hand synchronization on a single string. In this 4-measure study, execute strict alternating 16th notes (Down-Up-Down-Up) across frets 5-6-7-8, moving cleanly down strings 1, 2, 3, and 4. Focus on exact rhythmic evenness and identical volume between downstrokes and upstrokes.

patternNote.text: Rule: Strict alternation (D-U-D-U). 1 finger per fret: Index (5), Middle (6), Ring (7), Pinky (8)

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Set your metronome to 75 BPM. Keep your right wrist resting lightly near the bridge pins without anchoring rigidly. Every note must have equal punch and articulation.

exercises.title: Outside vs. Inside String-Crossing Drill
exercises.description: String crossing is where alternate picking breakdowns happen. In Bar 1, you practice 'outside picking' (downstroke on string 2, upstroke on string 1, where the pick moves outside the two strings). In Bar 2, you reverse the stroke to 'inside picking' (upstroke on string 2, downstroke on string 1, trapped between the strings).

patternNote.text: Bar 1 Outside: Down (str 2) ➔ Up (str 1) | Bar 2 Inside: Up (str 1) ➔ Down (str 2)

notation.title: Outside vs Inside String-Crossing Mechanics
notation.staveTitle: Isolating Outside and Inside Picking Transitions Between Adjacent Strings

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Notice how inside picking feels tighter and requires smaller pick excursions. Pay attention to pick slant: slant slightly downward when changing strings after an upstroke.

exercises.title: The Paul Gilbert String-Crossing Sextuplet Lick
exercises.description: This iconic 6-note sequence is Paul Gilbert's signature alternate picking workout. Spanning strings 2 and 1 in A minor, the lick forces you to navigate string changes on both downstrokes and upstrokes at rapid speed, building ironclad string-tracking coordination.

patternNote.text: Gilbert Sequence: [5-7-8 on str 2] ➔ [5-7-8 on str 1] ➔ [7-5 on str 1] ➔ [8-7 on str 2]

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Maintain strict down-up alternation throughout. Do not 'cheat' by using hammer-ons; every single note must be struck cleanly with the pick tip.

sections.title: 3NPS Scalewise Tracking, Chunking & Master Speed Etude

exercises.title: 3-Note-Per-String Ascending & Descending Grid
exercises.description: Because 3 notes per string is an odd number, your pick stroke reverses on every single string change: String 6 starts on Down, String 5 starts on Up, String 4 starts on Down, and so forth. Mastering this stroke reversal is the gateway to neoclassical and progressive metal shred.

patternNote.text: Stroke Inversion: Str 6 (D-U-D) ➔ Str 5 (U-D-U) ➔ Str 4 (D-U-D) ➔ Str 3 (U-D-U)

notation.title: 3-Note-Per-String Alternating Pick Grid
notation.staveTitle: Traversing 3NPS A Dorian Across All 6 Strings with Inverted Strokes

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Do not let upstrokes sound weaker than downstrokes. Accent the first note on each string slightly to anchor your rhythmic subdivision.

exercises.title: 4-Note Chunking & Directional Speed Drill
exercises.description: Speed on guitar is achieved through mental 'chunking'—processing a group of 4 notes as a single cognitive pulse rather than 4 separate conscious decisions. This drill ascends and cascades across strings using symmetrical 4-note cells.

patternNote.text: Chunking Mindset: Group 4 pick strokes into 1 mental trigger on the metronome click

notation.title: 4-Note Chunking Velocity Workout
notation.staveTitle: High-Speed 4-Note Symmetrical Chunking Across All Six Strings

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Practice in bursts: play one measure at maximum clean speed, stop on beat 1 of the next measure, relax your forearm completely, and repeat.

exercises.title: Neo-Classical Pedal Point Alternate Picking Run
exercises.description: Pedal point picking alternates continuously between a stationary drone note and a descending scalewise melody. In the style of J.S. Bach, Yngwie Malmsteen, and Randy Rhoads, this study tests your stamina, pick rotation, and string tracking at rapid tempos.

patternNote.text: Pedal Mechanics: Alternate continuously between High E (12.1) and moving scale degrees

notation.title: Neo-Classical Pedal Point Study
notation.staveTitle: High-Velocity Pedal Point Bouncing Across Strings 1, 2, and 3

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Keep your picking movement compact. The pick should only travel just far enough to clear the string, maximizing stroke economy.

exercises.title: The Master Alternate Picking Etude: Multi-String Velocity
exercises.description: This culminating 4-measure etude synthesizes all alternate picking concepts: 3NPS multi-octave sprints, outside/inside string crossings, rapid directional changes, and harmonic voice leading across Am - F - Dm - E7. Play through with pristine note separation and unwavering metronome lock.

patternNote.text: Complete Synthesis: 3NPS Ascending ➔ Outside/Inside Crossings ➔ Harmonic Resolution

notation.title: Master Alternate Picking Etude
notation.staveTitle: High-Velocity Multi-String Etude Across Am - F - Dm - E7

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Record your practice runs with a smartphone camera focused on your picking hand. Look for any unwanted tension or excessive motion, and aim for effortless, gliding economy.

tips.title: Picking Mastery Insights, Pitfalls & Daily Workout

items.title: 3 Mistakes That Kill Alternate Picking Speed
items: String Hopping: Lifting the pick away from the guitar body to jump over strings creates fatal wrist tension and caps your speed at around 100 BPM. Use pick slanting escape trajectories instead.
Forearm & Shoulder Tension: Tensing the arm locks the wrist joint, causing fatigue and strain. Your picking power must come from a relaxed, oscillating wrist.
Leading-Hand Desynchronization: When the fretting hand runs ahead of or behind the picking hand, notes become muffled. Always practice slow enough that both hands strike simultaneously.

items.title: Masters of Alternate Picking
items: Paul Gilbert: The gold standard of alternate picking; renowned for machine-gun precision, wide string skips, and flawless 16th-note string-crossing sequences.
John Petrucci: Dream Theater virtuoso who perfected the 3NPS chromatic speed drill and symmetrical chunking with surgical accuracy.
Al Di Meola: Pioneer of Latin and fusion picking; attacks strings with aggressive, muted palm bite and legendary sextuplet fury.
Steve Morse: Dixie Dregs and Deep Purple legend famous for strict alternate picking through complex, non-adjacent arpeggio lines with zero economy cheating.

items.title: The 15-Minute Daily Picking Workout
items: Block 1: Single-String Motor Calibration (5 min) - Play 16th notes on one string at 80 BPM, focusing entirely on relaxed wrist movement and minimal pick depth.
Block 2: Outside & Inside String Transitions (5 min) - Alternate between 2 adjacent strings, cycling 10 repetitions of pure outside picking and 10 repetitions of inside picking.
Block 3: 3NPS Velocity Bursts (5 min) - Practice 3NPS scale runs across all six strings in 4-note chunks, stopping cleanly on the downbeat of every second bar.
